title: Anaphylaxis in a child
stem: Paediatric resus. A 7-year-old girl (about 23 kg) ate a biscuit at a birthday party 15 minutes ago. She has a swollen face, a hoarse voice, wheeze and hives. HR 150, BP 72/40, RR 36, SpO2 91%. Her aunt is with her.

phases.title: Recognise
phases.goal: Monitoring on, then A to E yourself: is this anaphylaxis? A quick history from her aunt.

phases.title: Adrenaline
phases.goal: Help, position, IM adrenaline 1:1000 for her age, oxygen.

phases.title: Circulation
phases.goal: Still hypotensive: fluid for her weight.

phases.title: Reassess
phases.goal: Not better at 5 minutes: repeat; the plan if it is refractory.

phases.title: After
phases.goal: Tryptase, observation, discharge planning; explain to her aunt.

events.say: Her voice is fading and her lips are blue. SpO2 84%, BP 64/34.
events.untreated: She deteriorated and never got IM adrenaline.

events.say: Five minutes since the first adrenaline.

review.text: Antihistamine and steroid. Your notes still give IM/IV hydrocortisone and chlorphenamine as routine. RCUK (2021) removed both from emergency treatment: an oral non-sedating antihistamine for skin symptoms once stable, and steroids only for refractory reactions or ongoing asthma or shock.

Adrenaline strength. Your notes give '0.1 mL of 1:10,000' as an IM equivalent. 1:10,000 (0.1 mg/mL) is for IV use only; IM adrenaline is always 1:1000 (1 mg/mL). Mixing them up is a known cause of harm.
IM adrenaline dose. AHA/WAO give 0.01 mg/kg of 1:1000 (max 0.5 mg): 230 micrograms here. RCUK use age bands: 300 micrograms at 6–12 years. The script says both; the cart gives 300 micrograms.
Fluid bolus. RCUK: 10 mL/kg crystalloid in children; AHA PALS: 20 mL/kg. The station uses 10 mL/kg and reassesses.

notes:
Checked against the Resuscitation Council UK emergency treatment of anaphylaxis (2021, with the 2024 update on refractory anaphylaxis) and the RCUK 2025 guidelines.

IM adrenaline 1:1000 (1 mg/mL) into the anterolateral thigh: under 6 months 100–150 microgram; 6 months–6 years 150 microgram; 6–12 years 300 microgram; over 12 years 500 microgram (300 microgram if small or prepubertal). Repeat after 5 minutes if not improving. After 2 IM doses with ongoing respiratory or circulatory problems: refractory anaphylaxis — low-dose IV adrenaline infusion with expert help, and fluids (10 mL/kg crystalloid in children).

Antihistamines and steroids are no longer part of emergency treatment (RCUK 2021): non-sedating oral antihistamine for skin symptoms after stabilisation; steroids only for refractory reactions or ongoing asthma/shock. Your notes still list IM/IV hydrocortisone and chlorphenamine doses as routine; they are not scored here.

Your notes also give the IM dose as '0.1 mL of 1:10,000' as an equivalent: 1:10,000 (0.1 mg/mL) is for IV use only. IM adrenaline must be 1:1000; mixing them up is a known cause of harm.

Mast cell tryptase: first sample as soon as possible after treatment, second within 1–2 hours (no later than 4), third at 24 hours or at follow-up. Observe (6–12 hours depending on severity), discharge with two adrenaline auto-injectors, training and an allergy clinic referral.

Perfect script checked against the RCUK anaphylaxis algorithm, an AHA PALS checklist, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Added: anaphylaxis named with its criteria, airway help early, a history from her aunt, refractory anaphylaxis, salbutamol, antihistamine and steroid placed correctly, biphasic risk, and an explanation to the family.

Audit: the clock runs to the reassessment; you reassess at the patient, and what you find brings the next step due.

steps.label: Monitoring
steps.hint: Ask the nurse to put the patient on the monitor.

opts.t: Hello Yan, I'm the doctor. Monitoring on, please: ECG, blood pressure and SpO2.
opts.mark: Asks for continuous ECG, NIBP and SpO2 monitoring

steps.label: Assess
steps.hint: Airway, breathing, circulation problems with skin changes after a trigger: anaphylaxis.

ABC.r: Lip and tongue swelling, hoarse voice, soft stridor. "Airway involvement."
HR 150, BP 72/40, cool hands. "She's in shock."
Widespread urticaria, facial angioedema. "Skin changes after a food trigger: this is anaphylaxis."
ABC.mark: Names anaphylaxis: airway, breathing and circulation problems with skin changes after a trigger

steps.label: Talk to her aunt
steps.hint: Allergies, asthma, previous reactions, what was in the biscuit.

opts.t: I'm the doctor looking after Yan. Does she have any known allergies, asthma or previous reactions?
opts.tz: 我係照顧欣欣嘅醫生。佢有冇已知嘅敏感、哮喘，或者以前有冇試過咁嘅反應？
opts.r: She has mild asthma. She's never reacted like this. I think there were nuts in the biscuit.
opts.rz: 佢有少少哮喘。以前從來冇試過咁。我諗塊餅入面有果仁。
opts.mark: History: allergies, asthma and previous reactions

steps.label: Nurse
steps.hint: Help, including airway help; the trigger; how she lies.

opts.t: Call for help now, including an anaesthetist for her airway, and remove the trigger.
opts.mark: Calls for help, including airway help; removes the trigger

opts.t: Sit her up while her breathing is the problem; lie her flat with legs raised if she becomes faint.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: IM adrenaline 1:1000: 0.01 mg/kg (300 micrograms for 6–12 years) into the anterolateral thigh.

opts.t: Adrenaline 1 mg/mL (1:1000) 300 microgram (0.3 mL) IM, anterolateral thigh
opts.mark: IM adrenaline 1:1000 into the anterolateral thigh, correct dose

opts.t: High-flow oxygen, 15 L via a non-rebreather mask

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Still hypotensive: IV access and a 10 mL/kg crystalloid bolus, reassess.

At 5 minutes.t: Reassess her at 5 minutes: airway, breathing, circulation
At 5 minutes.early: Five minutes after the first dose.
At 5 minutes.r: Still wheezy, SpO2 92%, BP 78/42. "No better at 5 minutes: repeat the IM adrenaline."
At 5 minutes.mark: Reassesses at 5 minutes and finds no improvement

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Not better after 5 minutes: repeat the IM adrenaline.

opts.t: Adrenaline 1 mg/mL (1:1000) 300 microgram (0.3 mL) IM again
opts.early: Give the first dose time: 5 minutes.

steps.label: Reassess
steps.hint: Repeat at 5 minutes; refractory after two doses; salbutamol for wheeze; no routine antihistamine or steroid.

opts.t: If she's no better at 5 minutes, we repeat the IM adrenaline; reassess ABC every few minutes.
opts.mark: Plans to repeat IM adrenaline at 5 minutes

opts.t: If she's still unwell after two doses, that's refractory anaphylaxis: an adrenaline infusion with expert help.
opts.mark: Recognises refractory anaphylaxis: IV adrenaline infusion with expert help

opts.t: Nebulised salbutamol for any ongoing wheeze. No routine antihistamine or steroid: an oral non-sedating antihistamine for the skin once she's stable.
opts.mark: Salbutamol for wheeze; antihistamine and steroid not first-line

opts.t: Mast cell tryptase now, and again within 1 to 2 hours.
She needed two doses, so she stays for at least 12 hours: there's a risk of a biphasic reaction. Admit her.
Before home: two adrenaline auto-injectors, training, an allergy action plan, and an allergy clinic referral.
opts.mark: Discharge plan with auto-injectors and referral

steps.label: Explain to her aunt
steps.hint: What happened, what we gave, and what comes next.

opts.t: Yan has had anaphylaxis, a severe allergic reaction, probably to nuts. The adrenaline injections are working. She'll stay overnight, because it can come back.
opts.tz: 欣欣係出現咗過敏性休克，即係好嚴重嘅敏感反應，應該係對果仁敏感。打咗腎上腺素針而家有改善。佢要留院過夜，因為有機會再發作。
opts.mark: Explains to the family: anaphylaxis, treatment, overnight stay

script.say: Hello Yan, I'm the doctor. Monitoring on, please: ECG, blood pressure and SpO2.

Airway: lip and tongue swelling, hoarse voice, soft stridor: airway involvement. Breathing: wheeze, RR 36, SpO2 91%: bronchospasm. Circulation: HR 150, BP 72/40, cool: she's in shock. Skin: urticaria and angioedema. Skin changes after a food trigger: this is anaphylaxis.
Call for help now, including an anaesthetist for her airway, and remove the trigger. Sit her up while her breathing is the problem; lie her flat with legs raised if she becomes faint.
IM adrenaline 1:1000, 0.01 mg per kg, maximum 0.5 mg: for a 7-year-old, 300 micrograms, 0.3 mL, into the anterolateral thigh, now. High-flow oxygen, 15 litres via a non-rebreather.
Does she have any known allergies, asthma or previous reactions?
script.do: Mild asthma; never reacted like this; nuts in the biscuit.

script.say: She's still hypotensive: IV access, and a crystalloid bolus of 10 mL per kg, 230 mL, then reassess.
Reassess ABC every few minutes. She's no better at 5 minutes, so repeat the IM adrenaline, 300 micrograms.

If she's still unwell after two doses, that's refractory anaphylaxis: an adrenaline infusion with expert help. Nebulised salbutamol for any ongoing wheeze. No routine antihistamine or steroid: an oral non-sedating antihistamine for the skin once she's stable.
Mast cell tryptase now, and again within 1 to 2 hours. She needed two doses, so she stays for at least 12 hours: there's a risk of a biphasic reaction. Admit her.
Before home: two adrenaline auto-injectors, training, an allergy action plan, and an allergy clinic referral.
Yan has had anaphylaxis, a severe allergic reaction, probably to nuts. The adrenaline injections are working. She'll stay overnight, because it can come back.
